In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of mitochondria in the control of cell fate.
the role of the cytoskeleton, and in particular microtubules, in regulating mitochondrial distribution.
the mechanisms of redox signaling in the cell.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mitochondria are not only the powerhouses of the cell but also a key player in cell signaling.
hypoxia induces the perinuclear accumulation of mitochondria to increase the concentration of ROS in the nucleus and thus the expression of hypoxic genes.
mitochondria can be considered as a redox sensor and a signaling organelle, and that their intracellular location may be a key determinant in their function as such.
